item.title: Chip stocks retreat but AI spend advances; upcycle has room to run
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — AI Semis: Spending strong, investor concerns build AI capex has seen upward revisions for years, and estimates for many semiconductor stocks have followed. Positioning in the semiconductor index may have gotten excessive around the June highs, but there have also been less positive developments since, from cancelled IPOs to widening credit spreads for neocloud companies. Combined with continued concerns around open models and AI pricing, these developments have fueled investor fears about the pace of AI spending growth. Vivek Arya joins the podcast to discuss his latest views on semiconductors, what the group needs to resume its upward trend, the sustainability of memory pricing, and how developments in AI models and efficiency could impact chip demand. He also looks to past semiconductor cycles for clues on how much longer this upcycle may last. item.title: The Curious Calm of Credit Markets
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — It appears that credit investors have gotten most of what they’ve wished for over the last decade. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Research Andrew Sheets considers whether there could be unintended consequences. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley. ----- Transcript ----- Andrew Sheets: Welcome to Thoughts on the Market. I'm Andrew Sheets, Global Head of Fixed Income Research at Morgan Stanley. Today, how spooked should we be about the credit markets? It's Friday, October 30th, at 2pm in London. I grew up watching The Simpsons , and I've always had a soft spot for their Halloween episodes. One in particular that's burrowed pretty deep in my memory involves a cursed monkey's paw. It technically granted wishes to whoever held it, but with unintended consequences. For example, Lisa wishes for world peace, the entire planet disarms; and then aliens invade and take over. That sort of thing. Keep that monkey's paw in mind. Credit markets are going through their own jittery episode. After a long period of support, central banks are raising rates and shrinking their balance sheets. item.title: 276: Rewiring Retirement Around The World: What Can We Learn?
item.dc:creator: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock · The Bid — Retirement planning is being transformed around the world. As people live longer, traditional pension systems evolve and governments face growing financial pressures, individuals are taking on greater responsibility for their retirement savings and income. But with no single global model for retirement, what can different countries learn from one another? In this episode of The Bid, host Oscar Pulido is joined by Casie Maurer, Head of US Defined Contribution at BlackRock, and Helen Lees-Jones, EMEA Head of Global Consultant Relations and Institutional Strategy at BlackRock. Together, they explore how retirement systems are changing across the US, UK, Germany, Australia and Mexico, and how policymakers, employers and the financial services industry are responding to the challenges of an aging population. From the evolution of 401(k) plans and automatic enrollment to the growing importance of retirement income, the conversation examines how different markets are approaching retirement planning. Casie and Helen discuss the shift from traditional defined benefit pensions toward individual retirement responsibility, the role of capital markets in supporting long-term savings, and why…

item.title: Private Investment Grade: An Efficient Allocation for Endowments and Foundations
item.dc:creator: Apollo
item.description: Apollo · Apollo Insights & Outlook (web) — Endowments and foundations (E&F) face a particular portfolio construction challenge: meeting current spending needs while preserving the long-term real value of principal. In most cases, the capital base is perpetual, and the portfolio must support distributions year after year without impairing future purchasing power. For many E&Fs, the traditional barbell approach—cash on one side, illiquid equity on the other—may no longer be enough. Private IG can deliver investment-grade credit exposure through bespoke origination across corporate credit, asset-backed finance, and structured solutions. For endowments and foundations, that can mean high-quality income with a premium spread to public credit, alongside structural protections and limited correlation to traditional risk-seeking assets. Used selectively, Private IG can help institutions support spending needs while building a more balanced and resilient portfolio.

item.title: Cycle, Structure, Selection: Private Equity Portfolios for Today’s Market
item.dc:creator: Apollo
item.description: Apollo · Apollo Insights & Outlook (web) — Private equity deal and exit activity have picked up in 2026, but valuations remain elevated and the macro environment is still demanding. How is this shifting PE allocations? Diana Sands and equity product specialist Bryn Gostin dive into what's actually changed in the market, how drawdown and evergreen structures can play distinct roles in a portfolio and what it takes to construct a durable PE allocation when the old playbook no longer applies.
